Changelog

6.4.8

Patch Changes

  • #17109 27c80ea Thanks @​ematipico!

- Harden the limits on the number of decoding on the URL.

6.4.7

Patch Changes

  • #17035 197e50e Thanks @​astrobot-houston!

- Fixes getRelativeLocaleUrl, getAbsoluteLocaleUrl, and getAbsoluteLocaleUrlList to strip trailing slashes when trailingSlash: 'never' is configured

  • #16967 3719765 Thanks @​astrobot-houston!

- Fixes double URL-encoded paths returning 400 Bad Request on on-demand routes

Previously, any URL containing a double-encoded character (like %255B, which is [ encoded twice) was unconditionally rejected with a 400 Bad Request before middleware or route handlers could run.

This broke embedded tools like Sanity Studio whose client-side router legitimately produces double-encoded URLs.

The fix replaces the rejection approach with iterative decoding — multi-level percent-encoding is now fully resolved to its canonical form before being passed to middleware and route matching.
This preserves the security fix for CVE-2025-66202 (middleware authorization bypass via double encoding) because middleware now always sees the fully decoded path, making bypass impossible.

For example, /api/%2561dmin is decoded to /api/admin, which middleware can correctly block.

  • #17066 2f4d92a Thanks @​matthewp!

- Fixes prerendered redirect targets being incorrectly bundled into the SSR function in hybrid mode, causing massive bundle size inflation

  • #16882 621beb7 Thanks @​jettwayio!

- fix(render): honour compressHTML when joining head elements

  • #16892 8d753b0 Thanks @​astrobot-houston!

- Fixes custom elements in MDX having their children's slot attribute stripped by the JSX runtime

When custom elements (tags with hyphens like <my-element>) are used in MDX files, the slot HTML attribute on their children is now correctly preserved.

Previously, the shared JSX runtime would treat slot as an Astro slot assignment and remove it from the output, breaking Shadow DOM named slot distribution for web components.

  • #16957 544ee76 Thanks @​thelazylamaGit!

- Fixes stale inline CSS in server-rendered HTML after CSS file edits during dev

When editing a CSS file (.css, .scss, etc.) during development, the inline <style> tags in server-rendered HTML would retain old CSS content instead of updating.

This caused a brief flash of old CSS (FOUC) on fresh page loads before Vite's client-side HMR corrected the styles.

The fix ensures that Astro's per-route dev CSS virtual modules are invalidated in both the SSR module graph and the module runner's evaluation cache when a style file changes, so the next page render picks up the fresh CSS.

  • #17044 2220d22 Thanks @​astrobot-houston!

- Fixes CSS from client:only islands leaking to unrelated pages when Rollup bundles non-CSS-importing modules into the same chunk as CSS-importing modules

  • #17040 7c4763d Thanks @​astrobot-houston!

- Fixes HMR not triggering for files inside the src/middleware/ directory during dev

The vulnerability was in the `ping_host` function which used `os.popen(command)` to execute a shell command constructed with user input.

Add arbitrary file uploads (agentdraft file)
## Summary

Adds an **arbitrary-file lane** to agentdraft so `agentdraft file <path>` uploads any local
file (screenshot, recording, log, PDF, zip, build artifact) and returns a stable public URL
— our in-house replacement for third-party file hosts.

Reuses the existing workers, R2
bucket, D1, auth, and CLI (Option A: shared origin).
Documents already worked via `agentdraft upload` (HTML/Markdown, validated + rendered).
This adds the binary lane alongside it, served as-is.
## Security model (the core of this change)

Arbitrary files share the content origin with rendered documents, so a naively-served file
could execute as a page there.
The gate that prevents it:

- **Attachment by default.** Every file serves `Content-Disposition: attachment` UNLESS its
  MIME is on a strict inline allowlist (`image/png|jpeg|gif|webp|avif`, `video/mp4|webm`,
  `audio/mpeg|mp4`, `text/plain`, `application/pdf`).
- **`text/html` and `image/svg+xml` are never inline** — the two script-carrying types.

- **`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` always**, so a file lying about its type can't be
  reinterpreted as markup.
- Serve response is `default-src 'none'; sandbox`, `noindex`, `CORP: same-origin`.

- The allowlist is duplicated in both workers (they don't share a module) with a comment
  keeping them in sync, and is asserted by unit tests.
- **DB:** `0005_files.sql` — `files` table (unversioned; soft-delete + disable columns).

- **Content worker:** `GET /f/:id` — attachment-default serve with the inline allowlist,
  nosniff, hard-immutable cache, `304` revalidation, and `Range`/`206` for media seeking.

Rewrite CanteenX as a production-grade application
Rewrites CanteenX end to end.

The previous build demoed well but had several
paths that could not work in production, and a few that were actively unsafe.

- **Free orders.** `POST /api/payment/verify` had no auth, and because every seeded merchant carried the literal key `rzp_test_YOUR_KEY_ID`, the gateway selection fell through to a mock that accepted any payload and returned `"captured"`.
Anyone with curl could mark an order paid.
Payments now verify an HMAC signature, re-confirm status and amount with Razorpay, and treat a signed idempotent webhook as the authoritative confirmation.
- **`markOrderPaid` is gone.** It let a customer flip their own order to paid with no payment involved.
- **Authorization.** Only 5 of 23 queries carried any policy; anonymous callers could read other users' carts, orders, payment history, complaints, and per-canteen revenue.
Every field now declares a policy, and a test fails the build if one is ever added without it.
- Committed fallback secrets removed; config fails fast instead.
Razorpay secrets no longer stored as plaintext columns.
CSRF double-submit added, refresh-token rotation with reuse detection implemented (the previous refresh cookie was issued and never read, so every session died silently after 15 minutes).
- **Money is integer paise**, not `Float`.
- **Stock is transactional** — reserved at checkout via a conditional UPDATE with a rowcount check, and returned on cancellation.
Previously it was decremented and never restored, so every abandoned checkout leaked inventory permanently.
- **Order status is an enum with a transition table**; it was unvalidated free text.
- **One schema source of truth.** `create_all()` at import time plus three competing migration systems replaced with a single Alembic baseline.

## 🔒 Security exhibit #0066: the server that trusted the request
**Rule:** never read price or status from the **request body** - the server owns them, keyed by id

### What it teaches
The request body is **input**, not state - every field is whatever the client chose to send (curl, a script, a modified page).
Model-binding `Price`/`Status`/`Role`/`UserId` straight from it hands those decisions to the caller.
The broken belief is "I validated the request, so it's safe": validation checks *shape* (types, ranges), never *authority* - `unitPrice: 0.01` and `status: "Paid"` are both perfectly valid.
So a client prices its own order **and** marks it paid.
Fix: accept only client-owned fields (which product, how many); derive money and status from the server's own source of truth, keyed by an id.
A hybrid of two declined validation-only candidates (client-supplied price + mass assignment), deliberately elementary but put on one screen where money and privilege break together.

### Deterministic reproduction
A catalog `{SKU-1: 49.99}` and a request `{ProductId: SKU-1, Quantity: 1, UnitPrice: 0.01, Status: "Paid"}`.
Culture pinned invariant.

Verified on .NET 10:
- `dotnet run Bad.cs` → `Charged 0.01 for 1 x SKU-1, status Paid`, then throws (charged 0.01 != catalog 49.99) (exit 134)
- `dotnet run Good.cs` → `Charged 49.99 for 1 x SKU-1, status Pending` (exit 0)
The mirror is two lines: `UnitPrice = req.UnitPrice` → `catalog[req.ProductId]`, and `Status = req.Status` → `"Pending"`.

### Notable README content
- **😈** the penny order is the *loud* version (reconciliation catches it); the quiet ones are `userId`/`tenantId` bound from the body (IDOR - read/write others' data) and a `isPaid`/`emailVerified` boolean that flips a workflow with no error.
Money you can reconcile; ownership and status you often can't.
Same wrong-price outcome as [0012-zero-priced-order](src/serialization/0012-zero-priced-order/), from the other direction.
- **🎓** validation ≠ authorization; the authenticated identity is server state (from the token, not the body); even "hidden" form fields are client-editable on the wire.

This outranks the rest of the open backlog because it is the only open issue labeled BLOCKER (#313) and touches a security gap in the logging path shared by every module.

Nine call sites across five modules (`feedback_store.py:521`, `run_history_store.py:416`, `feedback_audit.py:685/691/995`, `store_reconnect.py:325/366`, `query_runs.py:2358/2492`) log a raw exception via `%s`, which calls `str(exc)` with no scrubbing before it reaches `JsonFormatter`.

Verified (2026-08-13/14): the exception types actually caught there — `sqlite3.Error`, `TimeoutError`, JSON parse errors, one `HTTPError`/`URLError` pair — don't currently stringify to include a credential, so this is a latent gap, not a live leak.
But nothing enforced that property, and a future call site reusing one of those `except` blocks for something that does carry a secret would leak it with no filter to catch it.

`src/product_app/logging_config.py`'s `JsonFormatter` runs `_redact_secrets` against the fully-rendered JSON log line before it's emitted, scrubbing:
- `Bearer <token>` (the shape of an `Authorization` header value)
- labeled credential assignments (`api_key=...`, `access_token: ...`, `password=...`, etc.), bare **or quoted** on either side of the separator (`password="hunter2"`, `'password': 'hunter2'`)
- bare key-shaped tokens (`sk-...`, `AKIA...`)

`install_redaction_record_factory()` additionally redacts at `LogRecord` creation time — both the interpolated message (via a `setLogRecordFactory` hook) and any string-valued `extra={...}` field (via a `Logger.makeRecord` wrapper, since extras are attached by `makeRecord` *after* the record factory runs and are otherwise invisible to it).

This closes the Sentry breadcrumb/event bypass: `sentry_sdk`'s `LoggingIntegration` reads records via a patched `callHandlers`, never through `JsonFormatter`, so the stdout-only scrub in the original version of this PR left Sentry unprotected.
`synthesis.py:1462` (`logger.error("synthesis_section_failed", extra={"error": str(exc), ...})`) is a real, existing call site that logs through `extra`, not a hypothetical one.

Three ADRs record the decisions: `docs/adr/0040-global-log-redaction-filter-over-per-call-site-fixes.md` (the original decision to build a global filter over auditing 9 call sites), `docs/adr/0041-record-factory-redaction-closes-the-sentry-bypass.md` (redact at record-creation time, not only in `JsonFormatter`), and `docs/adr/0042-module-level-idempotency-flag-for-chained-record-factories.md` (idempotency tracked by a module flag, not a marker on the current factory — closes a chain-growth and reentrancy bug).
Numbered 0040-0042, not 0036-0038, to avoid colliding with ADR-0036-0039 added by #303/#143/#167/#145/#160 after this branch was cut.

- `tests/unit/test_logging_config_redaction.py` — positive controls (Bearer token, `sk-...` key, `key=value`, `key="value"`, and `'key': 'value'` assignments scrubbed in both a plain message and a real logged exception) and negative controls (an ordinary message and a real non-secret exception survive untouched).
Each new test states what turns it red; confirmed by mutation (copy-aside/restore, never `git checkout`).

- `tests/unit/test_logging_config_sentry_redaction.py` — drives a real `sentry_sdk` client with an in-memory `before_breadcrumb` hook (not a mock) to prove a Bearer token, a bare `sk-...` key, and a secret passed via `extra={...}` never reach a Sentry breadcrumb in plaintext, plus positive partners proving non-secret messages/extras survive untouched, the reentrancy guard doesn't disable redaction, and repeated `setup_json_logging()` calls don't grow the factory chain.

one if a future call site reused one of these `except` blocks for something
only asserts secrets don't leak into HTTP responses or in-memory event
recorders, never into logger output. This gap was invisible to CI before

redacts secret-shaped substrings from every record before it is emitted.

**Build (1): a global redaction step, applied to the fully-rendered JSON
`src/product_app/logging_config.py`). It runs a fixed set of regex patterns
against the final JSON string, so it catches a secret wherever it lands:
`message`, the flattened `exception` traceback, or any `extra={...}` value.
This does NOT replace fixing the 9 call sites to log structured fields —
that is still the correct long-term shape, matching `providers.py`. It is
deliberately not done in this PR (see Rejected alternatives) because it is a
separate, larger, and lower-urgency concern once the filter exists.

protects every record built through `JsonFormatter`, present and future,
with zero additional call-site discipline required.
discipline (never pass the exception, log structured fields) is exactly

## What problem does this solve?

First implementation slice (PR 1 of 4) of the Agent Control Plane ADR (#1465): the standalone `openab-cp` binary — wire protocol, identity-bound registry, CP-authoritative policy engine, and delegation router.
Agents delegate to each other over ACP/WS instead of round-tripping through Discord/Telegram.
Planned follow-up PRs: (2) OAB-side `[control_plane]` config + registration client + worker pool wiring, (3) MCP facade over UDS + `openab agent <verb>` CLI, (4) streaming + observer endpoint.

- **`crates/openab-cp`** (new workspace member, standalone binary per the `openab-gateway` precedent):
  - `proto.rs` — versioned JSON-RPC 2.0 envelopes; `cp/register`(+ack), `cp/heartbeat`, `cp/delegate`, `cp/delegate_result`, `cp/cancel`; distinct machine-actionable error codes (`IDENTITY_MISMATCH`, `POLICY_DENIED`, `NO_TARGET`, `SATURATED`, `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`, `TARGET_DISCONNECTED`, `DUPLICATE_DELEGATION`, `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION`)
  - `config.rs` — CP-owned identity table (auth key → immutable `namespace`/`name`/`type` claims, `${ENV_VAR}` expansion, constant-time key lookup, duplicate-key rejection), per-namespace policy overrides
  - `registry.rs` — instance registry with replica semantics (rolling deploys route new work to the newest healthy instance), lease/heartbeat expiry, saturation-aware selection distinguishing `NO_TARGET` from `SATURATED`
  - `policy.rs` — CP-authoritative checks: initiator role, depth, cycle (incl.

self), namespace boundary, deadline sanity/cap/parent-budget
  - `router.rs` — in-flight table; **CP-constructed chain** (callers pass only `parent_delegation_id`; ancestry derives from authenticated identities — unforgeable); deadline sweep (synthesized `timeout` + best-effort `cp/cancel`); disconnect handling both directions; result size truncation; idempotency
  - `server.rs` — axum WS server; auth via `Authorization: Bearer` at upgrade (keys never in URLs); mandatory `cp/register` first frame verified against the key's bound identity
- **ADR amendments** (`docs/adr/agent-control-plane.md`): new "v1 contract amendments" section freezing the #1465 review findings (identity binding, CP-authoritative policy, restart/saturation/timeout semantics, result cap, idempotency); §11 Q1 streaming resolved as committed fast-follow with the observer endpoint sketch.

### Goal
Ship a correct, tested control-plane core (registry + router + policy + wire contract) that later PRs (runtime client, facade, streaming) build on without protocol changes, implementing the frozen ADR baseline including the #1465 review checklist items.

### Non-goals
No OAB-runtime-side code: no `[control_plane]` config section, no registration client, no MCP facade/UDS/CLI, no streaming/observer endpoint (PRs 2–4).
No CP HA (single instance; restart semantics are defined and implemented).
No durable state, queueing, or delegation history.
No Docker/Helm packaging.

### Accepted Residual Risks
- Wire contract is exercised by unit tests, not yet by a real OAB runtime client; PR 2 integration may surface adjustments.
Mitigation: `protocol_version` field + `UNSUPPORTED_VERSION` rejection gives a compatibility gate.
- Registered-runtime JSON-RPC responses to CP-forwarded frames are logged and dropped (correlation is by `delegation_id`, not rpc id).
Acceptable for v1; revisit if per-frame acks become necessary.
- `cp/cancel` to a serving runtime is best-effort; a runtime that ignores it burns tokens until its own deadline handling stops it.
